seoTitle: Free CRC32 and Adler-32 Checksum Calculator
metaDescription: Calculate the CRC-32 (IEEE) and Adler-32 checksums of your text as UTF-8, shown in hex and decimal. Free and runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Compute the CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) and Adler-32 checksums of your text at the same time. Each value is shown in hexadecimal and decimal.
why:
CRC-32 sits inside ZIP files, PNG images, gzip streams and Ethernet frames, and Adler-32 inside zlib. When you debug a file format, compare a checksum with a spec, or write a test for a parser, you need to know the right number for a given input.

This tool computes both for the UTF-8 bytes of your text and shows them as eight-digit hex and as an integer. The sample "123456789" is the standard check value, giving cbf43926 for CRC-32, so you can confirm that it matches your own implementation. These checksums catch accidental damage only; they offer no protection against deliberate tampering.
howTo: Type or paste the text to checksum.
Read the CRC-32 value in hex and decimal.
Read the Adler-32 value in hex and decimal.
Copy the form your format or test expects.

faq.a: The common IEEE 802.3 one, with polynomial 0xEDB88320 reflected, an initial value of all ones and a final XOR. It is the one used by ZIP, gzip and PNG. Other CRC-32 variants such as CRC-32C give different results.

faq.q: Can I use these for security?
faq.a: No. Both are error-detection codes that are trivial to forge on purpose. For tamper detection use a cryptographic hash like SHA-256, available in the Hash Generator.

faq.q: How do I check my implementation?
faq.a: Enter 123456789. The correct CRC-32 is cbf43926 and Adler-32 is 091e01de. If your code gives something else, check the byte encoding and the byte order of the output.
No, this page takes text, which is encoded as UTF-8 first. To check a file, use the File Hash tool for cryptographic digests.
